description:
V1.1.0
Major update, adding 18 aviation calculators
Ui remake and fixing bugs

MetarNow is a firmware for the Cardputer focused on aviation use. It gives fast access to METAR, TAF, airport info, alerts, decoded weather, and 18 aviation calculators, in a simple handheld UI designed for the tiny screen.
Setup is straightforward:
On first boot it walks you through sound on/off, Wi-Fi setup, and choosing a home station, controls. After that, you can instantly open your home airport by clicking ENTER or search for any other station.
Core usage:
-Open your home weather instantly
-Search another airport when needed
-Use TAB to cycle through views (METAR → TAF → alerts → detailed weather → airport info)
-Press R anytime to refresh data
Extra controls & shortcuts:
-On the search screen:
-ENTER with no input → goes to your saved home station
-FN + W → scan for Wi-Fi networks
-FN + S → open Settings

Calculators control:
Up/Down fields, Enter next/open, Tab modes, G graph where available

Back deletes input first, then returns when the field is empty
In Wi-Fi scan:
-R → rescan networks
Wi-Fi behavior:
-Automatically connects to saved network if available
Otherwise opens scan so you can connect to a new one
Settings let you manage:
-brightness, saved Wi-Fi, sound, and controls.

V1.1.0
Added a new icon-based main menu:

WX DATA | CALCULATOR | SETTINGS

Also improved scrolling animations and fixed saved WiFi behavior, so known networks connect again without asking for the password every time.
skip connecting to a wifi for offline use.

New Calculator section

This was inspired by feedback/ideas from my previous post. The new calculator section now includes 18 aviation calculators:

WCA / GS calculates wind correction angle, heading, ground speed, drift, and leg time. Includes graph view.
XWIND calculates runway headwind/tailwind and crosswind components. Includes graph view.
LEG TIME calculates leg time, distance, or required speed.
FUEL includes fuel conversion, required fuel, and endurance, with decimal input and AVGAS/JET-A1/JET-B selection.
ALTITUDE calculates pressure altitude and density altitude.
CLOUD BASE estimates cloud base from temperature, dew point, and field elevation.
DEW/RH calculates dew point or relative humidity.
CLIMB calculates top of climb distance/time or required rate of climb.
GLIDE calculates glide distance or altitude loss.
1:60 RULE calculates tra
ck error/opening angle and closing correction.
ETP/PNR calculates equivalent time point and point of no return.
IAS estimates indicated airspeed from TAS, pressure altitude, and temperature.
TAS estimates true airspeed from IAS, pressure altitude, and temperature.
MACH calculates Mach number and speed of sound.
GS ONLY is a focused ground speed calculator.
WCA is a focused wind correction angle and heading calculator.
BANK LOAD calculates load factor and revised stall speed in a bank.
DMMS calculates defined minimum manoeuvring speed from VS1 and safety factor.
--------------------

description:
Module Tester


A menu-driven test bench for the M5Stack Cardputer ADV (ESP32-S3) that lets you wire up and test M5Stack and third-party modules — radios, displays, GPS, RFID, IR, and audio.


Features


Modules menu — pick a unit and run its dedicated test screen:

  • CC1101 — Waterfall, Detect Freq, raw chip status, pin finder
  • NRF24L01 — chip status, 2.4GHz spectrum scan, pin finder
  • PN532 — NFC/RFID read
  • M5Stack RFID 2 — card read/test
  • GPS — live fix display
  • IR — capture, replay and manage IR signals (Flipper .ir format)
  • M5Stack LoRa Cap — LoRa + onboard GNSS
  • External Display — SPI display pin test, colour fills, Matrix rain and starfield test patterns
  • Speaker — plays RTTTL melodies (preloaded tune + your own .fmf files from SD), tone sweep, volume control, through the Cardputer ADV's onboard ES8311 codec

SD card browser — browse and manage files on the card directly from the device

Find chip pins — scans the shared SPI bus's spare GPIOs to help locate an unlabelled chip's wiring
Screenshot capture — Fn+S from anywhere saves a BMP of the current screen to the SD card
Per-module pin configuration — remembered on the SD card, no recompiling to change wiring


Hardware


M5Stack Cardputer ADV (ESP32-S3)

Whichever test modules you want to try: CC1101, NRF24L01, PN532, GPS, RFID 2, LoRa Cap, an SPI display, etc. Pins for each are configurable on-device.

name: MonoMesh
description:
# MonoMesh

**Standalone Meshtastic client for the M5Stack Paper Mono** — chat, node list and
offline maps directly on the e-paper device, with no phone, no Bluetooth and no
Wi-Fi required.

[![CI](https://github.com/andrecolz/MonoMesh/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/andrecolz/MonoMesh/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

Current release: **v1.0b (beta)**

## What it can do

- **Mesh messaging** — broadcast channels and end-to-end encrypted direct
  messages (X25519 + AES-256-CCM, Meshtastic 2.5+ PKI), ACK/NAK, retries and
  managed-flooding relay, with unread badges and message history on screen.
- **Node list** — name, model, MAC, PKI lock, RSSI/SNR and hop count; telemetry
  (device, environment, air quality), traceroute, waypoints received and
  NeighborInfo transmitted.
- **Offline maps** — a single `.mmap` container per region (recommended) or a
  PNG tile tree on MicroSD; pan, zoom, node pins, waypoints and "go to my
  position".
- **Touch keyboard** — compose messages with uppercase/symbols and a scrolling
  text field; quick menu and physical buttons for page navigation.
- **On-screen settings** — region, modem preset, frequency, TX power, hop
  limit, channel name and PSK, node identity and role, broadcast intervals,
  TX duty-cycle budget, rebroadcast mode, buzzer mode, timezone/RTC, clock
  orientation and storage info.
- **Power modes** — power off, standby with the radio always listening, giant
  clock, clock + RX; battery protection and configurable power-button action.
- **Works without MicroSD** — settings, keys and recent messages persist in
  NVS; the card adds full chat history, node database and maps.

## Offline maps

The tools generate tiles from a local `.osm.pbf` file (for example from
[Geofabrik](https://download.geofabrik.de/)), completely offline and without API
keys:

```bash
# one-time
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt

# one .mmap container for the area around a point (recommended)
python3 tools/mmap_converter.py --tui

Copy the resulting `.mmap` file into `/maps` on the MicroSD.

## License and attribution

GNU General Public License v3.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

MonoMesh is an independent implementation interoperable with the
[Meshtastic](https://meshtastic.org/) wire protocol; "Meshtastic" is a trademark
of Meshtastic LLC and this project is neither affiliated with nor endorsed by
Meshtastic LLC. Map data derives from **© OpenStreetMap contributors** (ODbL) and
the tiles must be attributed accordingly. Third-party components (map style,
clock font) are listed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

name: Multi-Tools ADV (Timer, Dados e Sorteio)
description:
O Multi-Tools ADV é o verdadeiro "canivete suíço" para o seu M5Cardputer. Desenvolvido para ser um utilitário de bolso diário, este aplicativo reúne quatro ferramentas essenciais em uma única interface limpa e direta. Ele é o companheiro perfeito para sessões de estudo focadas (técnica Pomodoro), medição de tempo em tarefas e, principalmente, para noites de jogos de tabuleiro com os amigos.

Seja substituindo dados perdidos de um jogo de RPG, sorteando letras para uma partida de "Stop/Adedanha" ou cravando o tempo de uma apresentação, este aplicativo elimina a necessidade de pegar o celular e se distrair com notificações.

Como Funciona a Dinâmica (Os 4 Módulos)

    Timer de Foco (Ajustável com Memória): Muito mais que um simples contador regressivo. Você ajusta o tempo exato que precisa direto no teclado. O grande diferencial é a Memória de Ciclo: se você configurar para 1 minuto (ou 25 minutos para um Pomodoro), quando o tempo acabar e o alarme tocar, basta apertar "Reset" e ele volta instantaneamente para a sua configuração personalizada, pronto para o próximo round sem precisar ajustar tudo de novo.

    Cronômetro de Precisão: Um medidor de tempo progressivo clássico. Ele exibe minutos, segundos e milissegundos, perfeito para registrar recordes de tempo de leitura, montagem de projetos ou atividades físicas.

    Rolar Dados (D6): Esqueceu os dados do jogo de tabuleiro? Este módulo gera rolagens 100% aleatórias. Você pode escolher rolar apenas 1 dado, 2 dados ou 3 dados simultaneamente na tela com o toque de um botão.

    Sorteio de Letras: Um gerador automático que puxa uma letra aleatória do alfabeto (A a Z) a cada aperto de botão. Indispensável para jogos de palavras clássicos em grupo.

Mapeamento de Controles e Atalhos

Menu Principal:

    Teclas 1, 2, 3 ou 4: Acessam os respectivos módulos.

    Tecla 0: Retorna ao Menu Principal de qualquer lugar do aplicativo.

Controles do Timer de Foco (Módulo 1):

    Tecla ENTER: Inicia (Play) ou Pausa o timer.

    Tecla R: Reseta o timer para o último tempo configurado por você.

    Tecla ; (ponto e vírgula): Adiciona +1 Minuto.

    Tecla . (ponto): Subtrai -1 Minuto.

    Tecla / (barra): Adiciona +10 Segundos.

    Tecla , (vírgula): Subtrai -10 Segundos.

Controles do Cronômetro (Módulo 2):

    Tecla ENTER: Inicia ou Pausa a contagem.

    Tecla R: Zera o cronômetro.

Controles dos Dados (Módulo 3):

    Tecla 1: Rola 1 dado na tela.

    Tecla 2: Rola 2 dados na tela.

    Tecla 3: Rola 3 dados na tela.

Controles do Sorteio de Letras (Módulo 4):

    Tecla ENTER: Sorteia e exibe uma nova letra aleatória na tela.

name: Muse-Gadget For Cardputer-ADV
description:
Muse-Gadget For Cardputer-ADV is experimental open-source firmware based on the Meta [Muse Gadget SDK](https://github.com/facebookincubator/muse-gadget-sdk/tree/main/esp32) that turns the M5Stack Cardputer-Adv into a portable Muse AI terminal. Users can start voice conversations directly from the device and read Muse's text responses on its display.

Key features include:

- **Portable Voice Q&A**: Hold `Space` or `GO` to record a question, then release the key to send the voice message through the paired Muse's control session. Muse transcribes and processes the message and displays its text response on the device.
- **Keyboard-Based Interaction**: Use `Esc` to open or close the menu or go back, the arrow keys to navigate, and `Enter` to confirm, providing fast control without a touchscreen.
- **Dedicated Device Access**: Start conversations, check connection status, and read responses without continuously using a phone. The complete conversation remains available in the Muse App.
- **AI Interaction Prototyping**: Developers can use the Cardputer-Adv keyboard, microphone, and display to create shortcuts, custom menu logic, and specialized interaction flows for portable AI tool prototypes.
- **Muse Pairing and Connectivity**: The Muse App handles pairing and Wi-Fi setup. Press `Enter` to confirm pairing and establish an encrypted communication session.

This is currently an experimental port. Because the Cardputer-Adv has no PSRAM, the firmware uses a reduced voice-input and text-response mode and does not support image display, spoken responses, the home-network tunnel, battery telemetry, or OTA updates. The firmware requires the Muse App, a Muse account, an SDK Token, and Wi-Fi connectivity. It is not a standalone offline AI model.

name: Muse-Gadget For StopWatch
description:
Dedicated firmware for M5Stack StopWatch based on the Meta [Muse Gadget SDK](https://github.com/facebookincubator/muse-gadget-sdk/tree/main/esp32). The firmware runs on the ESP32-S3R8 and provides board-level support for the M5Stack StopWatch's round touchscreen AMOLED display, audio codec, power management IC, and physical buttons.

Key features include:

- **Full On-Screen UI**: Displays Muse status, an animated avatar, connection status, battery information, response text, and settings on the 1.75-inch, 466 x 466 round AMOLED display.
- **Voice Interaction**: Captures voice through the built-in microphone and plays Muse's voice responses through the speaker. The blue upper-right button provides Push-to-Talk control.
- **Touch and Button Controls**: Supports touchscreen interaction and integrates the StopWatch's blue voice button, yellow speaker control button, and red power button.
- **Image Display**: Displays images sent by Muse and renders them for the round screen resolution.
- **Muse Pairing and Connectivity**: Pairs with the Muse App, connects to a home Wi-Fi network, and establishes an encrypted communication session. Device settings, Bluetooth configuration, and OTA updates are supported.
- **Power Management and Low-Power Operation**: Monitors battery and USB power status. When running on battery with the display off, the firmware powers down the display and audio circuits and enters Light Sleep until awakened by a physical button.

The hardware adaptation targets the M5Stack StopWatch with an ESP32-S3R8, 16 MB Flash, 8 MB Octal PSRAM, CO5300 AMOLED display controller, CST820 touch controller, ES8311 audio codec, single microphone, and AW8737A speaker amplifier.

A sonar fishing machine in your pocket.

The screen is an abstract sea: black water, cyan sonar returns, fish as drifting dots. You sit at a turret on the seabed — tilt the device and the gun follows your wrist. Fire, and the camera rides the shell out to the target: a clean hit bursts into coins, a big one shakes the screen, a break-out snaps the net and the fish bolts.

· Tilt-to-aim: how you hold it is where it points
· 9 species, from minnows to a shark, plus a diver who has no business being there
· Three cannon tiers — the heavy one punches through two fish at once
· Tidal schools, and a shark that scatters everything in its path
· Catch log: per-species counts, best score and peak coins, kept across sessions
· Two minutes idle and it sleeps; any key wakes it

name: NEXUXPAD
description:
NEXUS DEXOPAD PRO

O Nexus DexoPad Pro é uma aplicação que transforma o seu M5Stack Cardputer ADV num poderoso recetor de periféricos sem fios (Wireless HID Bridge). Ao ligar o Cardputer por USB a qualquer computador, ele cria instantaneamente um servidor Web local (via Wi-Fi ou Ponto de Acesso próprio). Basta aceder através do navegador do seu telemóvel para o transformar num verdadeiro centro de controlo produtivo.

Recursos Principais:

    Trackpad Inteligente: Suporte a gestos multi-touch para controlo suave do rato, toque para clicar (tap-to-click) e scroll com dois dedos.

    Controlo de Multimédia: Botões dedicados para reproduzir, pausar, avançar faixas e controlar o volume global do sistema de forma remota.

    Modo Apresentação: Um passador de slides elegante com botões gigantes e atalhos rápidos para dominar apresentações em PowerPoint ou Keynote.

    Teclado Completo: Introdução de texto sem atrasos e suporte nativo ao clássico layout de setas em "T invertido" e teclas de função (F1 a F12).

    100% Plug & Play: Não requer instalação de drivers no computador hospedeiro nem aplicações extras no telemóvel. Onde há uma porta USB, há controlo.


NEXUS DEXOPAD PRO

The Nexus DexoPad Pro is an application that transforms your M5Stack Cardputer ADV into a powerful Wireless HID (Human Interface Device) Bridge. By plugging the Cardputer via USB into any computer, it instantly hosts a local web server (either via an existing Wi-Fi or its own Access Point). Simply open your smartphone's browser to turn it into an ultimate remote productivity hub.

Key Features:

    Smart Trackpad: Multi-touch gesture support for smooth mouse movement, natural tap-to-click, and two-finger scrolling.

    Media Remote: Dedicated buttons to play, pause, skip tracks, and control the system's master volume from anywhere in the room.

    Presenter Mode: A sleek slide clicker featuring oversized buttons and quick shortcuts to master PowerPoint or Keynote presentations.

    Full Keyboard: Zero-lag text input, featuring a dedicated inverted-T arrow key layout and full function row (F1-F12).

    True Plug & Play: Requires no driver installations on the host computer and no extra apps on your phone. If there's a USB port, you're in control.

name: NNOs - NoName Operating System
description:
**Updated**
Added usb audio support (fn + o modal) / Barely tested, needs a powered hub afaik.

Significant rework:
- Runs on hybrid arduino3/espidf
- New logging system wired to fn + d, configured via fn+g
- SndRec32 can open pls file exclusively containing web radios links (mp3, 128kbps only), display a menu and hopefully play them correctly
- ImageViewer received png and jpg performance enhancement and bugfix
- DosEdit is more stable and capable
- Added Micropython (with capability to run .py files you would have created with DosEdit for example) and a REPL. Super experimental though.
- Added a MicroCLI to run some orphaned commands not found in apps
- Greatly enhanced IRCamera app for Thermal module (mlx90640)
- CardKB2 and ble keyboard support via dedicated apps
- STOrk app (mimic a stork toy that distord voice) buggy app nonetheless
- Latest Ardugurl BUT without IRAM_ATTR so lower performance than standalone (by design)
- few more modals, driver improvements etc... 

A snappy, all-in-one OS suite packing 20+ apps for your Cardputer!
Play Ardugurl and Chip8, or use DosEdit, SndRec32, Canary, and a REPL Calc.
Features advanced keyboard modes and global Fn-shortcuts.
Full disclosure: rushed release! Expect bugs, crashes, and weird UI quirks :) (use Esc, left arrow, del or reset if stuck !)
SD card heavily required. Download it, break it, and kindly report the bugs!

Acknowledgments:
Massive thanks to the developers of the libraries that make this possible (among others): M5Unified & M5Cardputer, ggwave (for data over sound), minimp3 (by lieff), JPEGDEC/PNGdec (by bitbank2), FastLED, and NimBLE-Arduino.

TL;DR:
NNOs (NoName Operating System) is a fast, all-in-one suite that turns your Cardputer into a proper pocket Swiss Army knife. I got tired of flashing different apps every time I needed a specific tool, so I packed over 20 of them into one highly responsive build.

I rushed this release (feel free to ask why). The experience isn't fully unified yet, the UI might jump around a bit depending on the app, and there are absolutely some crashes hiding in there. I still have to debug and polish things, but it's surprisingly usable. Don't depend on it for life-support, and kindly report bugs!
⌨️ Advanced Keyboard Modes & Global Shortcuts

Because diving into menus is slow, I've hardcoded global shortcuts and custom keyboard layers directly into the driver. You can use these anywhere in the OS.

Global Fn-Shortcuts (Hold Fn + Key):

    w: WiFi Modal

    z: BLE Modal

    y: Battery Modal

    k: Clock Modal

    l: LED Modal

    u: USB Modal

    j: Joystick Modal

    b: GPIO Button Modal

    d: Diagnostic Modal

    c: Cycle Display

    s: Silent Screenshot (Saves directly to SD)

    - / =: Volume Down / Volume Up

Hardware Sleep:

    G0 Button (Side): Press at any time to drop into instant light-sleep and save battery. Press any key to wake back up instantly.

Keyboard Modes (Tap modifiers to lock layers):

    Caps Lock: Double-tap Shift

    Fn Lock: Double-tap Fn

    Sticky Fn: Single-tap Opt. The very next key you press will use the Fn layer, then it auto-reverts to normal.

    Strict Navigation: Double-tap Alt. Maps the right-side symbol keys (;, ., ,, /) into a one-handed directional pad.


🛠️ App Survival Guide

Since some of these apps have custom controls, here is a quick guide on how to actually use them:

Cardputer Canary (Network Monitor)
A powerful uptime and status monitor. It loads a CSV file from your SD card. Your CSV needs at least an Alias and a Target, but can also specify Type (PING, HTTP, HTTPS, DNS), Payload, Headers, and Interval.

    Press m to toggle between the dense Matrix view and the detailed List view.

    Shows active UP/DOWN/WARN status and ping response times.
Example file:
Alias,Target,Type,Payload,Headers,Interval
ROUTER,192.168.1.1,PING,,,60
GOOGLE,google.com,PING,,,300
MY-SITE,example.com,HTTP,Example Domain,User-Agent:Cardputer/1.0,300
DNS-TEST,one.one.one.one,DNS,1.0.0.1,,60
BAD-URL,nonexistent.test,HTTP,,,60
HIGH-LAT,8.8.8.8,PING,,,5

SndRec32 (WinAudio)
A classic sound recorder.

    Use keys 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 to activate the top UI buttons (Seek Back, Seek Fwd, Play/Pause, Stop, Record).

    Press l to load a new file.

    It records 16-bit 8000Hz WAVs to a folder called sd:/Esprec32/. Stop playback to be able to record. It also plays MP3s.

REPL Calculator
A Read-Eval-Print-Loop calculator. Type an expression and press Enter.

    Supports variables (x = 5 + pi), hex conversions (toHex(255)), and math functions (sin(), sqrt(), f2c()).

    Holds your last result in the variable ans.

    Type help to see all available commands.

DosEdit
A text editor paying tribute to the MS-DOS days. Type your text normally.

    Press the MENU (or ESC) key to jump focus to the top menu bar where you can Save, Open, or Copy/Paste lines.

    Use arrow keys to navigate the dropdowns.

Icon Editor
Pixel art on the go.

    Use the arrow keys to move the cursor, and Enter to toggle pixels.

    Hit the MENU key to open the options to Save/Load BMPs, or export your drawing directly into a C++ byte array in sd:/icons/icon_code.txt.

Carlendar
An offline calendar viewer. Put a calendar.ics file on your SD root and let it parse the events.

    Use [ and ] to navigate backward and forward between months or days.

    Press t to jump back to today.

    Press j to jump to a specific date (YYYY-MM-DD), or s to text-search your events.

Image Viewer
Open a .jpg, .png, or .bmp via the file selector.

    Once the image is open, use the Left and Right arrow keys to instantly cycle through all other images in that same folder.

    Press Up to open the file selector again.

IR Camera
(Requires the MLX90640 unit).

    Press Enter to cycle through the temperature scales (Human, Fridge, Full range).

    Press Right (Forward) to toggle fullscreen mode.

name: NTRIP Client for M5Stack StickC Plus2
description: The program is an NTRIP client for the M5StickC Plus2 written in MicroPython. It connects to Wi-Fi and then to an NTRIP server to download RTCM correction data, which it forwards via UART to a GNSS receiver. It reads NMEA messages (GGA, GST), determines position, altitude, fix status (GPS, DGPS, FLOAT, RTK), and the number of satellites in use. It calculates the age of RTCM corrections and displays it as a progress bar. The screen shows coordinates, dE/dN deviations, timers for different fix modes, and Wi-Fi and NTRIP status. It includes automatic reconnect logic, timeouts, authentication error blocking, and sound alerts for key status changes.

name: Nesso_base
description:
Arduino firmware for the **Arduino Nesso N1** handheld controller — a
WiFi/BLE/LoRa-enabled base station that controls a remote robot platform over a
selectable wireless link: WiFi-UDP, TCP, BLE, or LoRa (CRC-checked NessoLink
RemoteFrame protocol with receiver failsafe). Features a 240×135px TFT display
with a multi-mode menu, battery monitoring, and up to **four simultaneous
control inputs** — Adafruit seesaw gamepad, M5Stack Mini JoyC HAT, M5Stack Unit
JoyStick2, M5Stack Unit Joystick v1.1, and the board's own BMI270 IMU as a tilt
stick — with one drive stick plus up to three aux sticks, a configurable device
order, per-stick orientation adaptation, calibration and deadzone settings, and
named controller profiles. Also: a BMI270 sensor screen (attitude, gyro rates,
raw axes), IR and 433 MHz RF remote control, RFID card scanning, Speaker Hat 2
(MAX98357A) audio, an experimental BLE HID gamepad mode, and a web-based file
manager.

Robot side: control frames are encoded by the **NessoLink** Arduino library —
install it from the IDE Library Manager (or `arduino-cli lib install NessoLink`,
source: github.com/ugursayar/NessoLink) and decode with `nessoDecode()`. The
library ships ready-made receiver examples for ESP32 (`RobotReceiverUDP/TCP/BLE`),
Arduino Uno R4 WiFi (`UnoR4ReceiverUDP/TCP/BLE`), and M5 Cardputer ADV + Cap
LoRa 1262 (`CardputerAdvLoRaReceiver`), so a robot can be up and driving with a
few lines around `applyMotors()`.

**Requires NessoLink 1.4.0 or newer on the robot.** A floor rather than an exact
pin — newer releases decode older frames unchanged, so installing the current
Library Manager version is always right. The floor is 1.4.0 because it tracks
what this build *can* emit, not what it emits by default: frames are v1/v2 out
of the box, but turning on **IMU TX** promotes every frame to v3 and **AUX3 TX**
to v4, and `nessoDecode()` rejects a version byte it does not know — it fails
closed, but it does stop, and the all-stop frame travels the same path. Both
rows default OFF precisely so this cannot happen by accident, and the on-device
toggles say which NessoLink version they need.

**Note:** flashing resets device settings (NVS) to defaults — your saved IR /
RF433 / RFID files, controller profiles and network config live on the
filesystem and are kept.

## What's new in v1.2.0

- **M5Stack Unit Joystick v1.1** (I2C `0x52`) joins the roster, alongside JoyStick2
  on the same Grove port
- **The built-in BMI270 IMU is a control input** — tilt the device to drive, with a
  selectable tilt range; on by default since the sensor is soldered to the board
- **New SENSOR screen**: attitude indicator, pitch / roll / yaw-rate, and raw
  accelerometer + gyroscope axes; tap to zero to your current hold
- **Configurable device order** — DRIVE / AUX 1 / AUX 2 / AUX 3 are handed out over
  whatever is connected, and unplugging a device no longer overwrites your choice
- **Controller profiles**: named snapshots of the whole mapping plus the robot's
  IP/ports, so switching rigs or robots is one tap
- **Screen lock** (on by default) — the Controller and Sensor screens hold the
  orientation you entered them in, so tilting never rotates the display or remaps
  the axes mid-drive or mid-reading
- RemoteFrame **v3** (transmitter IMU attitude) and **v4** (a third aux stick),
  both opt-in and both requiring a matching NessoLink on the robot
- **Guaranteed stop**: an explicit all-stop whenever the drive loop stops running —
  leaving the screen, opening settings, or losing the drive stick — retried until
  the transport accepts it
- Fixes: aux stick axes were transmitted transposed and at the wrong scale; the
  screen could come back empty after a long sleep (sprites moved to static buffers);
  the status header did not return when the controller settings panel closed

name: Nova Strike
description:
Nova Strike is an IMU demo firmware for the M5Stack Tab5 (ESP32-P4). It reads accelerometer and gyroscope data from the Tab5's built-in BMI270 or an external BMI270 module, and provides an IMU attitude view, a tilt test, and a tilt-controlled space shooter. The external module connects to Port A and can be a M5Unit DoF6, DoF9, or DoF10; the firmware probes I2C addresses 0x68 and 0x69 at boot.

The firmware is built with ESP-IDF 5.5.5 and LVGL 9.5, and renders the 3D fighter with a software 3D renderer. The main menu offers IMU TEST, TILT TEST and START GAME, and lets you switch between the built-in and external BMI270. The external module is detected only at boot; if none is found, the Tab5's built-in IMU is used.

In Tilt Fighter, tilt the device to steer the fighter, which fires automatically. Clear five waves and defeat the boss to enter endless mode; pickups include upgrades, healing, and a temporary weapon boost.

name: NoxPass
description:
# NoxPass

An offline password manager for the M5StickS3. Your passwords are encrypted on the stick (AES-256-GCM), protected by your PIN, and never leave it.

Plug it into any computer, enter your PIN with the two buttons, pick an entry, and the stick types it for you like a USB keyboard.

## Features
- Encrypted vault, PIN of 6 to 20 digits, nothing stored in the cloud
- USB keyboard (QWERTY by default, AZERTY in the settings)
- Everything controlled with two buttons, one hand
- Bridge: the stick creates its own Wi-Fi and a web page to manage your entries from a phone or PC
- Username / email presets, 19 two-color themes, auto-lock

## Quick start
Flash, press **A** at the owl, choose a PIN (**don't forget it**, it cannot be recovered).

[Full guide](https://github.com/git-psi/NoxPass/blob/main/START.md) | [Source code](https://github.com/git-psi/NoxPass)

name: NucleoOS: desktop + offline AI for Cardputer & ADV
description:
**Turn your Cardputer into a real computer:** a full desktop in your browser, 50+ native apps and games, and an AI assistant that works offline.

Type `nucleo-01.local` in any browser on your Wi-Fi and the Cardputer itself serves you a desktop: files, spreadsheet, paint, terminal, SSH, music and video, 40+ apps. In your hands, a fast launcher with big readable fonts and **ANIMA**, an assistant that answers, calculates, sets timers and opens apps with no cloud at all.

### Highlights
- **ANIMA offline assistant** in English and Italian (it can also use a model on your PC or in the cloud)
- **Web desktop** served by the device: 40+ apps in any browser on your network
- **50+ native apps and games**: Game Boy and Game Gear emulator, Tanks, Pinball, music and video player, voice recorder, IR remote, Wi-Fi and BLE tools
- **One binary for Cardputer and Cardputer ADV**: the board is detected at boot
- **5 languages**: EN, IT, ES, FR, DE
- **Safe A/B updates** with automatic rollback; also runs as a guest under M5Launcher

### Install
1. Burn this image (same file for Cardputer and Cardputer ADV).
2. On first boot the setup wizard joins your Wi-Fi and downloads the SD card content (web desktop, apps) by itself, or copy `nucleoos-0.7.3.0-sd.zip` from the GitHub release to a FAT32 microSD.
3. Open the address shown on the screen in your browser.

Free for noncommercial use (PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0); commercial use needs a license. Includes security-testing tools: authorized testing, research and education only.

Source, docs and release notes: https://github.com/indecenti/NucleoOs

name: Official GhostESP: Revival for M5Cardputer
description:
What's new (Merged Firmware .bin File):

Added

    Added wifistatus CLI command to show connection status and saved network info
    Added new wardriving and GPS info display view
    Added GhostLink split-channel wardriving helper mode (startwd --helper) with helper-to-primary observation streaming
    Added optional software NMEA RX backend (minmea_soft) for template-specific GPS routing constraints
    Added Factory Reset option to wipe NVS and reboot
    Added auto upload to WiGLE - @Play2BReal
    Added WiGLE manual upload browser in display settings with paged CSV list and per-file upload actions
    Added WiGLE stats popup in display settings with scroll and close controls
    Added WiGLE CLI commands: wigle files [page], wigle upload <filename>, and wigle stats - @Play2BReal, @jaylikesbunda
    Added control app updates - @tototo31
    Added Flipper Zero Companion App documentation - @tototo31
    Added SD JIT mounting for custom evil portal menu option
    Added hold to invert letter case on joystick select in keyboard view
    Added option to select custom portal for karma attack
    Add IO expander programmable button commands - @tototo31
    Added 'Cherry Blossom' and 'Soft Sand' themes

Changed

    'chipinfo' command now shows firmware version and enabled build features (Display, NFC, BadUSB, IR, GPS, etc.)
    Use country-appropriate channel list in main deauth task
    Improved GPS Info display with fix mode, satellites in view, and cleaner logging
    Moved multiple attacks and scans to separate files for maintainability
    Significantly optimised port scan memory usage
    Slightly increased IR Learn task size to prevent crash
    Improved BLE Spam
    Deauth: fixed 5GHz HT40 tuning, added burst loops, and removed rate limiting
    Reorganized settings menu into more categories
    Directly iterate to channels when deauthing multiple APs
    Optimised wardriving dwell times, added active probing and improved validation
    Wardriving now builds role-aware channel plans for split capture (primary 5 GHz, helper 2.4 GHz when both are available)
    Wardriving heartbeat now reports helper merge stats (helper=merged/received) for link visibility
    Reworked wardriving Wi-Fi dedupe into peek/commit flow to avoid consuming dedupe state before a successful CSV write
    Shortened delays for misc display menu building for more responsive feel
    Improved clock view responsiveness
    Increased BadUSB VSense delay to improve reliability of USB enumeration
    Improved CLI scan validation and status messaging for invalid durations and failed timed scans
    Improved CLI sd read/write/append reliability checks to report short writes and stream errors
    Improved task startup error handling for DIAL, Karma, Deauth, Beacon, EAPOL, DHCP Starvation, and SAE Flood
    Improved BLE capture startup flow to fail fast when handler registration or scan start fails
    Optimized PineAP detection memory model by lazily allocating detection tables at start and freeing them on stop
    Reworked PineAP detection logging to use a single queued worker task instead of per-detection task creation
    Reworked PCAP writer buffering to use a fixed static packet slot pool instead of per-packet heap allocations
    Reduced splash screen hold time from 2000ms to 900ms
    Refactored surface colors to be consistent across the UI
    Changed default screen timeout to 30s
    Miscellaneous fixes, improvements and refactors
    Fixed feberis pro spelling

Fixed

    Fixed station deauth channel lookup
    Fixed potential NULL dereference in command registration when strdup fails under low memory
    Fixed silent serial startup failures by validating queue and task creation in serial_manager_init
    Fixed race-prone stop behavior in SAE flood by waiting for task exit before freeing crypto context
    Fixed race-prone restart behavior in Karma and Beacon by waiting/cleaning lingering tasks on stop
    Fixed DHCP starvation reporting success while socket/send operations were failing
    Fixed select CLI parse errors that omitted the invalid token and improved index list boundary checks
    Fixed GPS latitude parsing for GLL sentences (was using 3-digit degree width instead of 2)
    Fixed BLE not initializing when selecting a flipper
    Fixed crash when deinitializing BLE
    Fixed BLE stop hangs by draining active scan callbacks before shutdown and reducing heavy callback work
    Potentially fixed "Connect to saved WiFi" resets on repeated use
    Fixed GPS satellites logic
    Fixed misc wardriving issues
    Fixed wardriving AP loss where entries seen before a valid GPS fix could be skipped later by premature dedupe mutation
    Fixed 5GHz deauthing
    Fixed crash when stopping deauth
    Fixed joystick repeat only working vertically
    Fixed evil portal JIT mounting
    Fixed crash on the Setup Wizard screen
    Fixed touch handler for the WiGLE help popup
    Fixed saving of WiGLE API credentials to mirror other setting saves
    Fixed listing large amounts of evil portals on displays
    Fixed crash starting karma attack
    Fixed 'stop' not stopping the karma attack
    Fixed joystick and touch input not checking if display is dimmed
    Fixed wardrive exiting when waking the display with a touch press
    Fixed NFC saved tag popup having vertically aligned buttons instead of horizontal
    Fixed Marauder v4 SD Card mounting

You can flash the bins with https://espressoflash.com/

name: Old Time Radio Player Live Internet Radio Retro Stream
description:
WiFi Internet Radio for the M5Stack Core1 Basic — a port of the excellent winRadio project by Volos Projects, re-skinned with a custom retro old-time radio aesthetic. 📻

Sound is not great. It is Old Time Radio, all of them have been converted from records, to reels, to tapes to probably multiple digital formats, over the last 80 years or so. Some shows may sound very poor. I recommend switching stations until a better sounding show comes on. 8 stations to choose from. 
Features
WiFi internet radio streaming 
Retro old-time radio UI skin
8 preset stations (ROKiT Radio Network classic/OTR streams, 48 kbps MP3)
Scrolling song/metadata ticker
VU meter bar graph
Bass / Treble / Volume controls
WiFi credentials stored in NVS via captive portal setup
Hold BtnA during 3-second boot window to re-enter WiFi setup
Button Mapping
Button	Normal Mode	Sound Settings Mode
BtnA (left)	Open sound settings	Exit back to radio
BtnB (middle)	Cycle station	Select next parameter
BtnC (right)	Cycle volume	Increase selected parameter

When you boot the device a Captive Portal will open to set up your WiFi connection. ON your phone or PC. IF it fails to open, turn off your moblile data and browse to 192.168.4.1 in your mobile browser WHILE connected to the CORE. 

Credits
Original project: winRadio by Volos Projects
Original hardware target: Waveshare ESP32-S3 with ST7789 240×240 display.
All core audio streaming logic, station management, and UI concept by Volos Projects.

Ported and Modified by Coreymillia

The main addition in V1.1 is a new companion build for the Cardputer ADV and Core2.

In this setup:
The Cardputer ADV acts as the controller

This makes it possible to run One More Floor as a two-device setup, with input handled on the ADV and the game displayed on the Core2.

name: OpenWiFi Scanner - Cardputer & ADV
description:
Works with both Cardputer models.

This tool continuously scans for open networks, searching for internet access, and generates a report of the surrounding Wi-Fi networks. It displays the detected networks, categorized by their security status.

SCREEN:
- Green: Indicates networks that provide open access to the internet.
- White: Indicates networks that are open without encryption but may not provide internet access.
- Orange: Indicates networks that use outdated or weak encryption, potentially at risk.
- Red: Indicates networks that are securely encrypted and protected.

LED:
- Green LED: Lights up when open networks or networks with web access are detected.
- Orange LED: Lights up when vulnerable networks are detected.
- Red LED: Lights up when only closed networks are found.

SPEAKER:
- One bip tone: Plays when a vulnerable network is detected.
- Two bip Tone: Plays when an open network is found.
- Melody tone: Plays when a web access network is available.


Disclaimer:

This tool is intended solely for educational and security purposes. It is designed to help users understand and assess the security of Wi-Fi networks. Do not use this tool to attempt unauthorized access to private networks. Unauthorized access to networks is illegal and unethical. Always obtain proper permission from the network owner before performing any scans or security assessments.

name: Oraculo
description:
O Oráculo Mágico transforma o seu M5Cardputer em um verdadeiro vidente de bolso! Inspirado no clássico brinquedo místico "Magic 8-Ball", este aplicativo é perfeito para ajudar a tomar daquelas decisões difíceis do dia a dia, prever o futuro ou simplesmente garantir boas risadas em uma roda de amigos.

O sistema conta com um gerador de aleatoriedade avançado (usando o ruído analógico do processador como "semente mística") para garantir que cada resposta seja única e imprevisível. Ele divide as respostas entre afirmações positivas, negativas e misteriosas, mantendo o suspense a cada consulta.

Como Funciona a Dinâmica
A interação com o Oráculo é simples, direta e envolta em mistério:

    A Concentração: O aplicativo exibe uma tela de espera mística. O usuário deve segurar o Cardputer, concentrar-se profundamente e fazer uma pergunta de "Sim ou Não" (mentalmente ou em voz alta).

    A Consulta: Ao pressionar o botão, o Oráculo entra em modo de transe. A tela exibe uma animação ou mensagem de "Consultando os astros..." para criar um breve suspense.

    A Revelação: O gerador de aleatoriedade escolhe uma das dezenas de respostas programadas (como "Sim, com certeza", "Minhas fontes dizem que não", ou "Nebuloso, tente de novo") e a exibe em destaque no centro da tela.

    Novo Ciclo: O Oráculo fica aguardando a próxima dúvida existencial do usuário.

Mapeamento de Controles e Atalhos

A interface foi desenhada para ser operada com um único dedo, mantendo o foco na brincadeira:

    Tecla ENTER ou Botão G0 (Botão lateral do M5Cardputer): Inicia a consulta aos astros e revela a resposta do Oráculo.

    Tecla ESC (ou DEL): Limpa a resposta atual e prepara a tela para a próxima pergunta.

name: OrcDial
description:
## OrcDial 0.1.0-beta.1 — Initial public testing beta

Turn your M5Stack Dial into an optional wireless controller for OrcSDR on the M5Stack Tab5.

- Dashboard-aware encoder, button and touch controls.
- Home VFO with tuning keypad and supported frequency, mode, step, span, filter and volume adjustments.
- FT8 receive controls when supported by the connected OrcSDR firmware.
- Secure pairing with persistent trust and automatic reconnection.
- Dial Settings for pairing, connection status, display and knob preferences.
- Firmware version and source identity shown in About and serial startup.

### Compatibility and pairing

Requires OrcSDR firmware with pairing protocol 4. The protocol-compatible receiver snapshot is OrcSDR nightly commit `0b8be74`; exact-build hardware pairing remains unverified.

Open **Settings → Accessories & Companion** on the Tab5 and **Dial Settings → Pairing** on the Dial. Compare the six-digit codes and confirm on **both devices**.

Do not mix this release with the earlier protocol-3 OrcDial prototype.

### Installation and beta limitations

M5Burner installation resets the Dial’s saved settings and pairing. Pair again after installation.

Firmware builds, automated tests and package checks passed. Exact-image installation, pairing, recovery, prolonged operation and independent security acceptance remain open. Please report issues with the VERSION and SOURCE shown in About.
author: hardcoreerik

name: OrcSDR
description:
# OrcSDR for M5Stack Tab5

Turn your **M5Stack Tab5** into a standalone software-defined radio with a compatible USB RTL-SDR dongle—no computer required.

## Features

- Touchscreen tuning for FM, AM, Shortwave, Airband, CB and other bands.
- Live spectrum and waterfall displays with audio playback.
- Dedicated dashboards for ADS-B aircraft tracking, P25, LoRa and POCSAG decoding.

## Supported dongles

Tested with **RTL-SDR Blog V4, V4L, V3c and Nooelec V5**. Reception depends on your antenna and local signals.

## M5Launcher compatibility

OrcSDR supports **C6 firmware 2.12.6 and 3.0.6**. The host and C6 version numbers do not need to match for supported Wi-Fi operation.

**Keep C6 2.12.6 to retain M5Launcher Wi-Fi/OTA.** The included C6 3.0.6 upgrade is optional; applying it stops M5Launcher's Wi-Fi/OTA functions.

## Installation

**M5Burner resets saved settings**, including Wi-Fi profiles, location and screen rotation.

A Windows settings-preserving installer is provided separately with release downloads. It leaves the settings area and existing C6 firmware untouched.

## Project

[Source code, documentation and releases](https://github.com/hardcoreerik/OrcSDR)

OrcSDR is beta software under active development.

description:
把一块桌面屏变成 1998 年的像素战场。

20 关小挑战 · 5 种塔（各 3 级）· 9 种敌人 · 8 种 BOSS 技能 · 本机大模型写就
· 魔性音效（一个音频文件都没有，全部是算出来的）

敌人从右边沿路走向你的基地，你只有 20 条命和有限的塔位。后面的关卡是岩地：
大片地面不能建塔，「好位置」本身就是要精打细算的预算 —— 难在要想，不难在抠门。

· 纯触摸：点底部选塔 → 点草地建塔 → 点已建的塔升级或卖出 → 右上角提前开下一波
· 8 种 BOSS 技能：自愈、现场产兵、死亡分裂、全场加速、沉默你的塔、偷你的金币、
  半血蜕甲变凶、周期性隐身
· 有一关是整屏一体的迷宫，也有一关是两条独立前线（守得住一边，守不住两边）
· 难度由一位真正的小学生测试员打出来的反馈定稿：不能轻易过关，但绝不需要唯一解

A pixel tower defence for M5Stack Tab5, written by a local AI model.

20 bite-sized levels · 5 upgradable towers · 9 enemy types · 8 boss abilities
· every pixel drawn by code, every sound synthesised — the app ships with no
image or audio files at all.

Build a maze with your towers and hold 20 lives. Later maps are rock fields:
most ground is unbuildable, so the good spots are a budget you have to spend well.

· Touch only: pick a tower → tap green ground → tap a built tower to upgrade or sell
· 8 boss abilities: self-heal, spawn, death-split, global haste, EMP, gold steal,
  armour molt, periodic ghosting
· Difficulty tuned from a real primary-school playtester's notes: never a
  single-solution puzzle, always retry-until-you-win

⚠️ 整包刷机会清空关卡进度与解锁记录；只想保住进度就用不擦除的升级方式 ⚠️

Turn a desktop screen into a 1998 pixel battlefield.

20 Guanxiao challenges · 5 types of towers (3 levels each) · 9 types of enemies · 8 types of BOSS skills · The local large model is written
· Magical sound effects (not a single audio file, all calculated)

Enemies approach your base from the right, and you only have 20 lives and limited tower slots. The next level is rocky ground:
A large area of ​​land cannot be used to build a tower, and a "good location" itself requires careful budgeting - it is difficult to think about it, not to be stingy.

· Pure touch: Click on the bottom to select a tower → Click on the grass to build a tower → Click on the already built tower to upgrade or sell → Click on the upper right corner to open the next wave in advance
· 8 BOSS skills: self-healing, on-site troop production, death split, full-field acceleration, silencing your tower, stealing your gold coins,
Half-blood sheds armor, becomes fierce, and periodically becomes invisible.
· One level is a maze that integrates the whole screen, and another level is two independent front lines (you can defend one side, but you can't defend both sides)
· Difficulty finalized with feedback from a real primary school student tester: not easy to pass, but never a unique solution

name: PORKCHOP
description:
--[ The Pig in the Machine

      They said pwnagotchi was dead.
      They said the ESP32 couldn't do it.
      They were wrong about both.

      A piglet woke up inside your Cardputer.
      It learned to sniff the spectrum.
      It learned to hunt the handshakes.
      It learned to track the clients.

      And somewhere along the way... it started keeping score.

      50 ranks. 10 class tiers. 64 achievements. Buffs that stack.
      The more you hunt, the stronger it gets.
      The longer you walk, the more it remembers.
      Your crimes become experience points.

      This is not a tool. This is a companion.
      A pocket-sized accomplice with moods, opinions, and a temper.
      It judges your network choices. It mocks your signal strength.
      It celebrates when you capture. It sulks when you don't.
      It watches the weather. It counts your steps.
      It demands challenges. Three per session. No excuses.

      You don't use PORKCHOP.
      You raise it.

      And when they wipe your flash, when they nuke your NVS,
      when they think they've reset you to zero...

      The pig remembers.
      The pig always remembers.


  --[ What Lives Inside

      [*] OINK MODE - Active WiFi hunt. Channel hopping. Handshake capture.
          Automatic PMKID extraction. Surgical deauth. Disassoc on demand.
          Your BOAR BROS stay protected. The rest are prey.

      [*] DO NO HAM - Passive mode. Zero TX. Ghost protocol.
          The pig watches. The pig waits. The pig still catches PMKID.
          Jah bless the patient sniffer. Irie.

      [*] HOG ON SPECTRUM - Real-time 2.4GHz RF visualization.
          Gaussian lobes. Channel overlap. Vulnerability markers.
          Press Enter. Hunt clients. Watch the arrows change.
          Proximity tracking. Vendor fingerprinting. Targeted deauth.

      [*] SGT WARHOG - GPS wardriving with WiGLE export.
          Every network. Every coordinate. Every building you pass.
          The map grows. The leaderboard awaits. OSCAR MIKE.

      [*] PIGGY BLUES - BLE notification storm.
          Apple. Android. Samsung. Windows. All of them.
          Phantom AirPods. Ghost earbuds. Endless popups.
          The library is OPEN.

      [*] BACON MODE - Fake beacon broadcaster.
          Your SSIDs. Your rules. Channel 6. Maximum confusion.
          Hide and seek, but nobody asked to play.

      [*] PIGSYNC - ESP-NOW encrypted device sync.
          POPS talks to SON. Porkchop feeds Sirloin.
          Bounties dispatched. Intelligence shared. The family eats.

      [*] PORKCHOP COMMANDER - WiFi file server.
          SD card access from any browser. Norton Commander layout.
          Upload. Download. Manage your loot. porkchop.local

      [*] WPA-SEC INTEGRATION - Distributed cloud cracking.
          Upload handshakes. Wait for results.
          Their GPUs, your passwords.

      [*] WiGLE INTEGRATION - Upload wardrives. Flex rank.
          The leaderboard knows your name. Or it will.

      [*] THE GRIND
          50 levels. SH0AT to B4C0NM4NC3R. 10 class tiers.
          64 achievements. 3 session challenges per boot.
          Hidden unlockables. Secret titles. Permanent buffs.
          The grind persists. Even through M5 Burner.

      [*] THE PIGLET
          A mood system. An avatar with feelings.
          It blinks. It walks. It judges. It sulks.
          Weather rolls in. Stars come out at night.
          The pig has a rich inner life.
          Your mental health was never our department.


  --[ Installation

      Flash at 0x0 via M5 Burner. Insert SD card. Boot.
      The pig awakens. The hunt begins.

      Previous XP will be restored from SD if available.
      New users start at LV1. Everyone starts somewhere.


  --[ Legal Fiction

      Educational and authorized security research ONLY.

      You already knew that.
      You're going to do what you're going to do.
      The pig doesn't judge. The law does.

      Don't be stupid. Don't get caught.
      And maybe don't hunt networks you don't own.


  --[ Credits

      Developed by: 0ct0
      Fueled by: 3am commits and questionable decisions
      Mascot: A cartoon pig with security clearance

      https://github.com/0ct0sec/M5PORKCHOP
      https://buymeacoffee.com/0ct0


                                the pig is watching.
                                the pig is waiting.
                                the pig remembers.

                                      oink.

  ==[EOF]==

description:
### PORTAL.HACK DEMO Firmware

#### Introduction
This demo version of the PORTAL.HACK firmware is designed for security demonstrations and experimental testing. It includes a limited selection of advanced features, such as a depowered RF jammer, the Windows BLE Bad-USB attack, and various test WiFi and BLE functions. This firmware is developed for use with the M5StickC Plus and M5StickC Plus 2 devices, leveraging the capabilities of the ESP32 microcontroller through the Arduino IDE.

#### Included Features

1. **RF Jammer (Depowered)**
   - **Description**: Temporarily disrupts nearby radio signals in a controlled and limited manner.
   - **Usage**: Ideal for testing the effectiveness of RF security countermeasures in controlled environments without causing extensive interference.
   - **Hardware**: Requires the MX-RM-5V receiver module connected to pin 25 and the FS1000A transmitter module connected to pin 26.

2. **Windows BLE Bad-USB**
   - **Description**: Utilizes the M5StickC device to execute "BadUSB" attacks via Bluetooth.
   - **Usage**: The device creates a Wi-Fi network that you can connect to, then access the link http://172.0.0.1/ to input commands, which will be executed when the M5StickC is connected to a Windows PC via USB.

3. **WiFi and BLE Test Functions**
   - **WiFi Scan**: Scans for nearby WiFi networks and displays details such as SSID, signal strength, and security protocols.
   - **BLE Scan**: Scans for nearby Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) devices, showing available devices and their characteristics.

#### Note
This firmware is intended for professional, educational, and demonstration purposes only. Unauthorized use of these features can violate laws and regulations. Always use responsibly and ethically.

name: Palnagotchi for M5 Atom S3(R) Dev Kit
description:
A friendly unit for those lonely Pwnagotchis out there. It's written to run on the M5 Atom S3(R) Dev Kit.

This is a fork of viniciusbo's Palnagotchi for the M5 Cardputer.

He reverse engineered the Pwngrid advertisement protocol and made it possible for the Cardputer to advertise to the Pwngrid as a Pwnagotchi. All brain policy parameters that could negatively impact AI learning were removed from the advertisemenet data.

The Pwngrid works by sending Wifi beacon frames with a JSON serialized payload in Wifi AC headers, containing the Pwnagotchi's data (name, face, pwns, brain policy between others). That's how nearby Pwnagotchis can detect and also learn each other. By crafting a custom beacon frame, this app can appear as a Pwnagotchi to other Pwnagotchis.

name: Paper S3 epub reader with usb disk mode
description:
EPUB e-book reader for M5Stack Paper S3.
Reads .epub files from the SD card.
Supports bookmarks, table of contents, adjustable font size,
and page progress.

Includes extended Latin characters (Czech, Slovak, Polish,
etc.).
Upload books via built-in USB disk mode.

Usage:
- Place .epub files in /books/ folder on the SD card.
- Group multi-volume series into subfolders of /books/
  (for example /books/Dune/). Subfolders are shown in
  the library as collections; tap to open, then tap
  "Back to library" to return to the root list.
- Tap a book title to open it.
- Swipe left/right to turn pages.
- Swipe up to open the menu (both in library and while
  reading). Works even when the SD card has no books —
  you can always reach Settings.
- Use Prev/Next buttons to browse pages when there are
  more books than fit on screen.
- Tap page number in status bar to go to a specific page.
- Tap bookmark icon in status bar to toggle a bookmark.

Library menu:
- Power off
- USB disk mode
- Settings
- Clear cover cache
- Clock

Reader menu:
- Font size (7 levels)
- Display refresh mode (Balanced / Fast / Quality)
- Images on/off (supports progressive JPEG; oversized
  images show a placeholder)
- Chapters (with bookmarks)
- Search
- Go to furthest read position
- Back to library
- Power off

Settings:
- Dark mode — inverted display (white text on black
  background) for comfortable night reading.
- Cover on power off — shows the book cover on the e-ink
  display when powering off.
- Hourly battery refresh — wakes the device every hour
  while powered off to redraw the lock screen with an
  updated battery %. Off by default; shortens battery
  runtime. A user alarm always takes priority.
- Auto power off — automatic shutdown after inactivity
  (off, 5–30 minutes).
- Flip display 180° — manual portrait orientation flip.
- Auto-rotation — IMU-based automatic orientation detection.
- Sync clock (NTP) — connect to WiFi to sync time.
- Alarm — set an alarm that wakes the device from sleep.

Search:
- Full-text search with on-screen keyboard.
- Diacritic-insensitive (matches č as c, etc.).
- Tap a result to jump to it with highlight.
- Navigate between results with Prev/Next bar.

USB disk mode:
- Connect to PC via USB-C.
- The SD card appears as a flash drive.
- Tap screen or eject on PC to exit and reboot.

Footnotes:
- Footnote markers are displayed inline as superscript
  numbers.
- Tap a marker to show the footnote text in a popup.
- Tap anywhere to dismiss.

Clock:
- Large clock display with current time, date, UTC offset,
  last NTP sync time, and alarm status.
- Tap anywhere to return to library.

Alarm:
- Set hour and minute (24-hour format).
- Wakes the device from deep sleep at the scheduled time.
- Beeps periodically until dismissed or auto-dismissed
  after 2 minutes.

description:
GameBoy emulator for M5PaperS3
- Supports only DMG, no GBC support yet
- Runs up to 60fps with dynamic frame skipping, runs close to full speed in many titles
- Supports sound output via internal buzzer
- Supports quick save/ quick load

Usage:
- Put your games in the SD card
- Select the game in the main menu
- Always remember to press SAVE after you saved inside the game. The SAVE button also saves a snapshot/ save state
- Press LOAD to load the previous snapshot/ save state
- Press anywhere in display area to force clear the screen (only during gameplay)
- The sound engine can be selected in the main menu: PCM (best audio quality, but rather quiet due to hardware constraints), Polyphony (Much louder, probably sounds funny though), and Mute

- 📰 **资讯早报**：IT之家 RSS 科技精选，每日 10 条

🌙 真·2mA 待机，续航 25~50 天；墨水屏不闪烁、不烧屏，常亮一整年。

English: Turn your 4" Spectra 6 full-color eInk into an all-in-one desk terminal — lunar calendar & weather, tech news RSS, spaced-repetition flashcards, Pomodoro, voice memos & dashboard. Fully offline Chinese TTS + voice assistant (long-press C), ~2mA ultra-low-power standby. Burn once, enjoy for years.

name: PaperDIY Reader
description:
A Kindle-style e-reader for the M5Stack PaperDIY. Reads EPUB and TXT books from the SD card with crisp anti-aliased text, saves your place in every book and resumes where you left off.


Features

  • Library home screen: cover grid (covers pulled from your EPUBs) with a progress bar per book; sort by recent, title or author
  • Beautiful text: Literata or Atkinson Hyperlegible, 5 sizes, adjustable spacing and margins with live preview; accented letters, Greek and real typographic quotes
  • Navigation: table of contents, bookmarks, go to %, "pages left in chapter"
  • Fast page turns: only the parts of the screen that change are refreshed (~0.2 s), with an automatic clean-up refresh every few pages
  • Sleep screens: your book's cover, five 16-grey generative designs, your own pictures, or random
  • Wi-Fi & files (radio is only on while this screen is open):
    • Join the reader's own PaperDIY-XXXXXX network (QR code on screen), or set up your home Wi-Fi and use http://reader.local
    • Upload books, manage the SD card (folders, rename, move, delete, download)
    • Turn any photo into a screensaver: cropped and dithered to the panel's 16 greys right in your browser
  • Extras: Conway's Game of Life and a sleep-screen gallery


Controls

Top keyBottom key
Click (reading)next pageprevious page
Click (menus)updown
Holdopen / select / menuback / library menu

Hold both keys 1.5 s to sleep. Power button: click to wake.


Getting started

  1. Put .epub / .txt files in a books folder on a microSD card (or upload them over Wi-Fi later).
  2. Flash, insert the card, and pick a book.

Flashing this image resets the reader's settings; books on the SD card are kept.


Open source (MIT): https://github.com/malonestar/paperdiy-reader

name: PaperDIY_ImagePush_Web_IDF
description:
## User Instructions

1. Power on PaperDIY and wait for startup.
2. Connect your phone or computer to Wi-Fi `PaperDIY-PNG` with password `paperdiy`.
3. Open <http://192.168.4.1/> in a browser.
4. Select an image, check the preview, and tap **Upload**.

Use PNG or JPG images up to `2.4 MiB`, with a maximum width and height of `4096` pixels. JPG
must use the standard Baseline format; Progressive JPG is not supported. Images are scaled
proportionally and centered; large images are reduced and small images are not enlarged. The
last uploaded image is kept on the device.


## 使用说明

1. 给 PaperDIY 上电，等待设备启动。
2. 手机或电脑连接 Wi-Fi：`PaperDIY-PNG`，密码：`paperdiy`。
3. 浏览器打开 <http://192.168.4.1/>。
4. 选择图片，确认预览后点击 **Upload**。

上传图片需为 PNG 或 JPG，文件最大 `2.4 MiB`，宽高最大 `4096` 像素。JPG 需使用普通
Baseline 格式，不支持 Progressive JPG。图片会按屏幕比例缩放并居中，过大的图片会
缩小，较小图片不会放大；设备会保留最后一次上传的图片。

name: PaperDarkRoom
description:
小黑屋 / A Dark Room —— 墨水屏放置生存游戏

经典文字放置游戏《A Dark Room》(Doublespeak Games) 的 M5PaperS3 原生固件移植，采用官方简体中文文本，12px 点阵中文字体渲染。

玩法：从一间黑屋、一堆将熄的火开始——添柴、生火、吸引流浪者、建造小屋、分配工人、经营贸易站，看着村落在灰白的屏幕上慢慢生长。造出罗盘后踏上「漫漫尘途」：整备背包，走进 61×61 格的程序生成荒原——探索地标、遭遇战斗、攻克矿山，活着回村把战利品和地图落袋；

📦 移植进度：当前版本 v0.10.1，Phase 1 + Phase 2 内容完整（生火间 / 村落 / 贸易站 / 随机事件 / 漫漫尘途 / 荒芜世界 / 战斗 / 14 类地标，含完整地穴地牢与矿山经济闭环）。Phase 3（坠毁星舰）已在规划，后续版本通过本页更新推送。

为墨水屏而生：

- 深度睡眠架构，待机以周计；睡眠期间村民持续生产，唤醒后离线收益自动结算——放置玩法与墨水屏天作之合
- 荒原征途每一步自动落盘：途中随时放下设备，断电即暂停，唤醒后从原地继续
 - 触摸交互：短按按钮即选择触发，顶部页签切换页面；有消耗的按钮直接标注本次花费与收获
- 存档自动写入 microSD 卡（需插卡），断电不丢——世界地图与征途进度也在卡上

烧录说明：完整镜像，烧录地址 0x0，适用于 M5PaperS3（16MB Flash）。首次启动自动开始新游戏；Phase 1 旧版本存档自动向后兼容。设备通过 RTC 记录时间，建议保持电池充足。

开源固件（游戏内容 MPL-2.0，上游为 doublespeakgames/adarkroom），源码见 GitHub 链接。
author: yibo.wang
description_en:
small dark room / A Dark Room —— Ink screen placement survival game

Classic word placement game《A Dark Room》(Doublespeak Games) of M5PaperS3 Native firmware migration，Use official simplified Chinese text，12px Bitmap Chinese font rendering。

How to play：from a dark room、一堆将熄of火开始——Soeshiba、Make a fire、Attract homeless people、construction shed、Assign workers、Run a trading post，看着village在灰白of屏幕上慢慢生长。After making the compass, set foot on「long dusty road」：Prepare your backpack，walk into 61×61 格of程序生成荒原——Explore landmarks、encounter battle、Conquer the mines，Return to the village alive and pocket the loot and map；

📦 Migration progress：Current version v0.10.1，Phase 1 + Phase 2 Complete content（Make a fire间 / village / trading post / random events / long dusty road / desolate world / fighting / 14 Class landmark，Contains complete underground dungeon and mine economic closed loop）。Phase 3（crashed starship）Already planning，Subsequent versions will be updated and pushed through this page.。

Born for ink screen：

- deep sleep architecture，Standby in weeks；Villagers continue to produce while sleeping，Offline earnings are automatically settled after waking up——放置How to play与墨水屏天作之合
- Every step of the wasteland journey is automatically placed.：Drop off your device anytime on the go，Suspend when power is off，After waking up, continue from the same place
 - touch interaction：Short press button to select trigger，Top tab switch page；有消耗of按钮直接标注本次花费与收获
- Automatic writing of archives microSD Card（需插Card），Not lost even when power is off——世界地图与征途进度也在Card上

Burning instructions：full image，Burn address 0x0，Applicable to M5PaperS3（16MB Flash）。Automatically start a new game on first launch；Phase 1 Old version archives are automatically backward compatible。Device passed RTC Record time，It is recommended to keep the battery sufficient。

Open source firmware（Game content MPL-2.0，The upstream is doublespeakgames/adarkroom），See source code GitHub Link。

name: PaperKlipp
description:
PaperKlipp is a lightweight touch UI for M5Stack Paper S3 that connects to a Klipper/Moonraker server over Wi-Fi. It shows live printer status (file name, state, progress, temps, fans, coordinates, print time/ETA/total) and provides touchscreen controls for common actions: preheat presets for bed/nozzle, homing, heaters off, movement/extrusion with selectable step size, toggles (light, filament sensor), and basic job control (start file, pause/resume, cancel with confirmation).

On first boot it runs a setup wizard that scans nearby Wi-Fi networks, lets you enter the password and Klipper host:port (plus optional API key) using an on-screen keyboard, and stores everything locally in flash (no SD card needed). It also includes reconnect/setup buttons and visual press feedback optimized for e-ink.

name: PaperMono Launcher
description:
PaperMono Launcher is a hardware-validated stable Launcher distribution for the M5Stack PaperMono.

It provides PaperMono-specific stability improvements, optimized E-Ink interaction behavior, firmware browsing, protected payload installation and boot, and reliable return-to-Launcher recovery.

### Highlights

- Native M5Stack PaperMono support
- Optimized SSD1677 E-Ink refresh policy
- Smooth menu and firmware-browser interaction
- Touch / button / SD / front-light support
- Firmware inspection and protected payload installation
- Payload boot and return-to-Launcher recovery
- Standalone ESP32-S3 application installation
- Support for eligible simple single-app FullFlash wrappers (F1-v1)
- Unsupported coupled multi-partition FullFlash packages remain blocked

### Quick Start

After flashing:

1. Power on PaperMono.
2. Enter Launcher from the boot selector.
3. Use the touch screen or side buttons to navigate.
4. Open the SD / firmware browser to inspect firmware files.
5. Eligible firmware will show the Install option.
6. After booting an installed Payload, use the supported return/recovery flow to return to Launcher.

### Firmware Compatibility

PaperMono Launcher does not treat every `.bin` file as safe to install.

For eligible F1-v1 FullFlash wrappers, only the validated embedded ESP32-S3
application is installed into the protected payload partition. The complete
FullFlash image is not written to the device.

### Project

Project repository:

https://github.com/MingRZou/PaperMono-Launcher

PaperMono Launcher is based on the open-source M5 Launcher
[bmorcelli/Launcher](https://github.com/bmorcelli/Launcher) project.

The initial PaperMono port was developed by adapting and extending Launcher's
existing M5Stack PaperS3-oriented implementation for the M5Stack PaperMono
hardware platform, followed by PaperMono-specific hardware adaptation,
stability work, and real-device validation.

### Important

- This is an independent community-maintained project, not official M5Stack firmware.
- This stable release is intended for M5Stack PaperMono only.
- Not every `.bin` file is installable through Launcher.
- FullFlash compatibility is intentionally conservative for device safety.

---

PaperMono Launcher 是面向 M5Stack PaperMono 的实机验证稳定版 Launcher。

它针对 PaperMono 提供了稳定性增强、优化后的墨水屏交互体验、固件浏览、受保护的 Payload 安装与启动，以及可靠的 Return-to-Launcher 返回和恢复功能。

### 主要特性

- 原生支持 M5Stack PaperMono
- 针对 SSD1677 优化的 E-Ink 刷新策略
- 更流畅的菜单及固件浏览交互
- 支持触控 / 按键 / SD 卡 / 前光
- 固件检查与受保护的 Payload 安装
- Payload 启动及返回 Launcher 恢复流程
- 支持独立 ESP32-S3 应用固件安装
- 支持符合条件的简单单应用 FullFlash 包装固件（F1-v1）
- 对不支持的多分区耦合型 FullFlash 固件继续保持阻止安装

### 快速使用

烧录完成后：

1. 启动 PaperMono。
2. 在启动选择界面进入 Launcher。
3. 使用触控或侧边按键进行菜单操作。
4. 进入 SD / 固件浏览器查看固件文件。
5. 只有通过兼容性与安全检查的固件才会显示 Install 选项。
6. 启动已安装的 Payload 后，可通过支持的返回 / 恢复流程重新进入 Launcher。


### 固件兼容性

PaperMono Launcher 不会将所有 `.bin` 文件都视为可以安全安装的固件。

对于符合 F1-v1 条件的 FullFlash 包装固件，Launcher 只会提取并安装其中
经过验证的 ESP32-S3 应用到受保护的 Payload 分区，不会将整个 FullFlash
镜像直接写入设备。

### 项目地址与来源

项目仓库：

https://github.com/MingRZou/PaperMono-Launcher

PaperMono Launcher 基于开源项目 M5 Launcher
[bmorcelli/Launcher](https://github.com/bmorcelli/Launcher)。

PaperMono 的初始移植是在已有的 M5Stack PaperS3 实现路径基础上，
针对 M5Stack PaperMono 特殊硬件进行适配和扩展，随后进一步完成了 PaperMono
专用硬件支持、稳定性优化以及实机验证。

### 说明

- 本项目为独立社区维护项目，并非 M5Stack 官方固件
- 当前稳定版本仅面向 M5Stack PaperMono
- Launcher 不会接受所有 `.bin` 文件进行安装
- 为保证设备安全，FullFlash 兼容策略保持保守

name: PaperOS v1.3 - Cardputer OS
description:
PaperOS v1.3 - A standalone operating system engineered specifically for the M5Stack Cardputer.

PaperOS turns your Cardputer into a compact workstation and retro-gaming suite, featuring a custom windowless launcher, a full-featured Lua 5.4 environment, an on-device offline LLM, and an ecosystem of native applications.

Key Features:
System & Tools: File Manager with enhanced image viewing (pan/zoom/rotate), Paint, 3D Mesh Editor (.obj), Notes, Calculator, Clock, and Piano.
Connectivity & Web: Tabbed HTML/CSS web browser with file downloading alongside a built-in App Store to fetch Lua apps directly from GitHub over Wi-Fi.
Media & Audio: Folder-agnostic Music Player with WAV and MP3 playback across the entire SD card.
Emulation & AI: Hardware-accelerated NES/GB/GBC and Arduboy game emulation, combined with an on-device offline LLM (myAI).
Developer Environment: Integrated Lua 5.4 console exposing direct hardware controls (GPIO, I2C, Canvas Drawing, Sound, and Timers).

What's New in v1.3:
Rewritten Web Browser: Upgraded to a lightweight HTML/CSS layout engine. Features parsing for style blocks (colors, bold formatting, alignment), headings, lists, tables, dynamic redirects, 3 independent tabs with history, in-page search, and image downloading to SD.
Dynamic Lua Wi-Fi Power Management: Wi-Fi now automatically powers down during Lua execution—reclaiming 40–70 KB of RAM—and seamlessly reconnects only when a script invokes network calls (net.get, net.post, net.connect, net.scan).
Lua Runtime Optimization: Unused standard modules (package, os/io, utf8, debug) have been stripped to permanently reduce memory overhead, and os.stack() has been added for real-time task-stack monitoring.

Requirements:
A FAT32-formatted SD card is required on first boot. Additional assets (PaperEMU.extension for emulation and model.bin for AI chat) as well as the updated API documentation (paperos_lua_reference_v1_3.txt) are available in the project repository.

name: Periscope OS: Wifi Attacker Radar
description:
## Tactical Manual: M5StickS3 Wireless Reconnaissance & Spectrum Analyzer Firmware

This updated firmware elevates the M5StickS3 into a unified, passive 
**Electronic Intelligence (ELINT) Station and Live RF Spectrum Visualizer**. Operating entirely passively without transmitting a single RF signal, the device monitors local 2.4 GHz airspace, providing immediate visual feedback on spectrum utilization while tracking, identifying, and logging wireless threats (Deauthentication and Disassociation frames).

---

## Technical Description

The architecture is divided into four highly synchronized core subsystems that manage real-time radio telemetry, digital signal processing, spatial orientation, and data logging.

### 1. Broad-Spectrum RF Visualizer & DPI Sniffer Engine

The single-core 2.4 GHz radio driver is configured for **Promiscuous Mode**, bypassing hardware MAC filters to ingest the raw environment. The sniffer callback handles a dual-pipeline workload:


* **The Spectrum Pipeline:** Unlike previous builds, the radio ingests *every single ambient packet* (Data, Control, and Management frames). Each packet strike exponentially drives the amplitude of the corresponding channel bar on the dashboard.

* **The Deep Packet Inspection (DPI) Pipeline:** The engine simultaneously filters for malicious management frames (Types `0xC0` and `0xA0`). Upon discovery, it performs real-time disassembly to extract the Attacker's MAC, Victim Client MAC, Access Point BSSID, and the 802.11 Disconnection Reason Code.

* **OUI Vendor Profiling:** The first three bytes of a flagged attacker MAC are parsed through an expanded internal lookup table to automatically identify offensive hardware categories (*Espressif/Flipper Zero devices, Raspberry Pi nodes, Alfa long-range cards, Hak5 gear, or Realtek rigs*).

### 2. Live Instrument Dashboard (Landscape Split-Screen)

The UI leverages a landscape layout ($240 \times 135$ pixels) to construct a high-fidelity tactical dashboard divided down the center by a structural pixel boundary.

* **Left Half (Spatial Sonar Disk):** Houses the retro-phosphor circular radar sweep. The sweeping beam simulates a classic CRT display with a 5-layer ghosting decay trail. Active threat sources are plotted as intense glowing blips (a white hot core surrounded by a blood-red aura bloom) that dynamically scale their distance from the crosshairs based on signal strength.

* **Right Half (Equalizer Spectrum Analyzer):** Replaces the historical waterfall with a live **volumetric frequency distribution graph** across Channels 1–11.

* **Peak-Hold Physics:** Floating above each channel bar is a single-pixel **Peak RSSI Tick Line**. When a burst of energy occurs, the tick snaps to the absolute signal power level ($\text{dBm}$) and decays slowly over time, capturing the physical proximity of intermittent or hidden transmitters.

* **Phosphor Dots:** Sitting directly above the spectrum box are 11 micro-indicator pixels. The dot corresponding to the radio core's active channel lights up bright green, providing a minimalist view of the channel hopper's location.

* **Reactor Core Battery Gauge:** Taps into the AXP2101 power management chip, rendering battery life as a vertical analog reactor core rod on the far right edge of the screen.

### 3. Spatial Inertial Processor (Body Shielding Math)

Because omnidirectional antennas lack directional intelligence, the firmware implements an internal calculus integration loop to execute **RF Body Shielding** tracking.

* **Angular Velocity Integration:** The code sample updates the 6-axis IMU (BMI270) to poll raw horizontal rotation velocity from the Z-axis gyroscope (`data.gyro.z`). It computes change-in-time ($dt$) and integrates it to calculate your precise physical heading relative to your boots.

* **Vector Locking:** When your body acts as a physical barrier dampening radio waves behind you, the code continuously compares incoming threat power levels. It binds the strongest peak RSSI value with your physical yaw heading, locking that coordinate line as the primary threat vector on the display.

### 4. Operational Modalities & The Captain's Logbook

* **Target Lock Mode (Button B Click):** Isolates a specific attacker's MAC address profile. The sniffer instantly discards all ambient network chatter to track that single signature across frequencies. The UI drops its green theme for an active tactical cyan layout and frames the target blip inside an automatic rectangular locking reticle.

* **Silent Running Mode (Button A Hold):** Deactivates the display backlights and mutes the speaker completely. Telemetry translates entirely to the internal haptic motor (`GPIO 44`). The motor generates clean haptic pulses that vibrate faster as your body rotates directly into the threat vector line.

* **Proximity Perimeter Breach:** If an active target breaches a critical proximity threshold ($\ge -42\text{ dBm}$), a master priority flag overrides standard operations. The screen flashes blood-red, the haptic motor holds a continuous hum, and the speaker blasts a dual-frequency acoustic naval klaxon horn.

* **The Captain's Log (SPIFFS Database):** Discovered threat metrics are compressed into single, pipe-delimited (`|`) strings and saved to the internal flash filesystem. The Logbook screen parses these data fields to compile standalone, scrollable interactive intelligence sheets.

---

## Directions for Field Operation

### UI Navigation Map & Button Layout

```
             ┌────────────────────────────────┐
             │       [LANDSCAPE MODE]         │
             │                                │
    [B] ─────┤  [RADAR DISK]   │ [SPECTRUM]   │ ◄─── [A] (Main Face Button)
 (Side Button) │   (TRACKER)     │ [HUD DATA]   │
             │                                │
             └────────────────────────────────┘

```

#### 1. Home Radar View

* **Button A - Single Click:** Toggles **Channel Lock**. Instantly freezes the background hopper on the active frequency. Use this the moment you see an active spike on the spectrum visualizer to park the radio core on that frequency.

* **Button A - Press & Hold:** Toggles **Silent Running**. Instantly blacks out the screen and silences audio for haptic-only tracking.

* **Button B - Single Click:** Toggles **Target Lock**. If a threat is actively attacking nearby, clicking this captures its MAC, drops a target box around the blip, and screens out all other wireless activity.

* **Button B - Press & Hold:** Leaves active tracking and drops down into the **Captain's Logbook Deck**.

#### 2. Captain's Logbook View

* **Button A - Single Click:** Cycles forward through saved threat sheets (`SHEET 01/12`, `SHEET 02/12`, etc.) to view individual target assets.

* **Button A - Press & Hold:** Permanently purges and deletes the log registry database from the flash storage.

* **Button B - Press & Hold:** Exits the log deck and re-engages active sonar navigation sweeps.

---

### Executing a Tactical Spectrum Sweep & Fox-Hunt

1. **Broad Airspace Assessment:** Power on the unit. Watch the right-side instrument panel. The vertical bars will bounce dynamically to show ambient traffic density on each channel, while the peak tick lines will register the relative proximity of local routers and client devices.

2. **Threat Acquisition:** If an offensive tool begins executing an injection attack nearby, the outer screen boundaries will flash red, a glowing threat blip will map to the left radar grid, and the speaker will begin chirping.

3. **Locking the Signature:** Note the active channel frequency where the equalizer bar is spiking into the red zone. Click **Button A** to lock your channel hopper to that frequency, then click **Button B** to lock the radar tracking core onto that specific attacker's MAC address profile.

4. **The 360-Degree Sweep:** Hold the M5StickS3 tight and flat against your solar plexus. Rotate your body slowly in a complete circle.

5. **Vector Localization:** When your back is turned to the adversary, your chest blocks the signals; the sonar chirps will slow down to a crawl and the blip will drift away. As you turn and face directly toward the physical location of the threat, the signal passes unhindered. The real-time spectrum bar will maximize, the peak tick will lock to the roof of the grid, the radar blip will snap close to the center crosshairs, and the audio chirps will escalate into a rapid-fire continuous tone.

6. **Closing Distance:** Move forward along that straight-line path vector. If the on-screen telemetry flips to `VCTR: CLOSING` and the pitch rises, you are closing the physical gap to the transmitter. If the device triggers a flashing **BREACH PERIMETER** klaxon blast, the asset machine is in your immediate physical room.

name: Philips Hue Zigbee Extender
description:
Open-source firmware converting the ultra-compact **M5Stack M5NanoC6** (ESP32-C6FH4) development board into a **Philips Hue Range Extender (Router)**.

Because the Philips Hue Bridge does not officially support generic Zigbee range extenders, this project emulates an **RGB + CCT Color Dimmable Light** (`GLEDOPTO GL-C-008P`) operating in **Zigbee Router (ZCZR)** mode. It seamlessly joins your Philips Hue Bridge network, acts as a full Zigbee signal repeater across your house, and provides physical hardware actuation!

### ✨ Features
- 🌐 **True Zigbee 3.0 Router (Range Extender):** Routes mesh traffic at the IEEE 802.15.4 layer and supports up to 20 child end devices in the Hue network.
- 💡 **Native Philips Hue Bridge Pairing:** Embeds the required Hue / ZLL Trust Center Key (`81:42:86:86:5D:C1:C8:B2:C8:CB:C5:2E:5D:65:D1:B8`) and `app_device_version = 1`, ensuring seamless discovery by Hue Bridge.
- 🎨 **Full RGB + CCT Color Support:** Full color wheel control (CIE 1931 XY gamut with automatic wide-gamut normalizer) and color temperature slider (6500K Cool White to 2000K Warm Candle) directly on the onboard WS2812 LED.
- 🔌 **Grove Actuator (GPIO 1 & GPIO 2):** When turned ON in the Hue app, Grove signal pins (GPIO 1 and GPIO 2) are driven to `HIGH` (3.3V) to trigger external relays, MOSFETs, or actuators. When turned OFF, they return to `LOW` (0V). Note: Pin 3 (+5V) of Grove Port A is continuously powered from USB VBUS.
- 🔘 **Front Button (GPIO 9):**
  - **Quick Click (< 1s):** Toggles the lamp state locally (ON/OFF) and reports back to the Philips Hue Bridge.
  - **Long Press (5s):** Clears Zigbee NVRAM/NVS credentials, unpairs from the current network, and reboots in pairing mode.
- 🚦 **LED Status Machine:**
  - **Pairing / Searching:** Blinking blue every 1s (500ms ON / 500ms OFF).
  - **Connected:** Solid blue for 2s, transitions to solid green for 3s, then enters normal operation.
  - **Normal Operation:** Matches selected Hue color, temperature, and brightness.
